messages:
Elaine: Emergency hotfix ready for embed-route auth token leak. Image: gcr.io/redwood/serve:hotfix-auth-2026-03-23-v3. Need expedited approval to push to prod within 15m. Plan: 10% canary for 10m -> metrics check -> 50% -> 100%. If error_rate > 0.5% or p95 latency +10% rollback. Requesting quick +1s. @ops-oncall please standby :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: deploy request received: image=hotfix-auth-2026-03-23-v3, target=prod/embed-route, strategy=canary(10%,10m)->50%->100%. Runbook: /runbooks/embed-auth-hotfix. To approve run: `/deploy approve 1824680123 --fastpath` or `/deploy start 1824680123 --canary 10m`.

Mike: acked, i'm on smoke. I'll watch traces + logs. :thumbsup:

Raj: quick question — does this change any client-facing schema?

Elaine: no schema change. Small token-scrub fix inside auth path. Verified on staging and eu1. Release note draft: "Fix token refresh race on embed route causing 401s under load." Link: https://docs.internal/releases/2026-03-23-hotfix-auth

Kelsey: ops checklist: cordon 1 node in canary pool? also set alert on embed-5xx increase to 0.4% for fast rollback.

ops-oncall: @Elaine i'm watching infra, standby. If SLO breach, i'll call rollback and trigger incident.

Mike: +1 for fastpath. Run smoke cmds: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer test' https://prod.embed/...` and validate 200 100x.

Elaine: executing `/deploy start 1824680123 --canary 10m --image hotfix-auth-2026-03-23-v3` now. Pin noted in release manager: image pinned to deploy id 1824680123.

deploy-bot: canary_started: 10% traffic -> 3 pods. Canary spans us-west1 and eu-west1. Monitoring hooks: traces, p95, error_rate, auth-401-rate.

deploy-bot: Canary metrics @ +5m: p95 +3%, error_rate 0.35%, auth-401-rate back to baseline.

Raj: seeing a small uptick on traces but looks like client retries clearing. continuing to monitor.

deploy-bot: Canary metrics @ +9m: p95 +11%, error_rate 0.82% (threshold 0.5%). Alarm: embed-route error_rate > threshold.

Kelsey: :warning: hitting rollback threshold. ops-oncall, do we want soft rollback (drain canary) or full rollback to previous image (gcr.io/redwood/serve:release-2026-03-20-v19)?

ops-oncall: Rollback full. Triggering now.

deploy-bot: rollback_command: `kubectl set image deployment/embed-route embed-service=gcr.io/redwood/serve:release-2026-03-20-v19 --namespace=prod` starting rollback sequence.

Mike: running post-rollback smoke. expect 200x.

deploy-bot: rollback_complete: traffic restored to previous image across all nodes. Canary pods terminated.

Mike: post-rollback checks: 200 OK x100, p95 back to baseline, error_rate 0.12%. Good.

Elaine: thanks all — hotfix aborted after canary. I've pinned the failing image to the incident record and added build artifacts. Will open a revert/patch PR and schedule a deeper root cause. Follow-up: postmortem and next steps in #incidents.

Raj: thanks for the quick run. Notes: reproduce under high parallel refreshes; I'll capture traces and a minimized repro.

Kelsey: filing rollback note and release note update now.

ops-oncall: all systems stable. Closing rapid response loop. :white_check_mark:
